headline: Meta shares sank nearly 7% as free cash flow turned negative
body: Meta shares fell nearly 7% on Thursday, and free cash flow came in at a negative $2.12 billion in the third quarter. Meta said it expects full-year capex of $135 billion to $145 billion, raising the bottom of the range from $130 billion. CNBC says the spread on its five-year credit default swaps reached all-time highs.
note: For finance people, the credit side is where this shows up: the spread on Meta's five-year credit default swaps reached an all-time high while the capex range moved up.

evidence.text: Meta stock sank almost 7% Thursday as free cash flow turned negative and the company raised the floor of its expected capex spend.
Meta shares slumped nearly 7% on Thursday as the social media giant showed negative free cash flow in its third-quarter earnings and raised the floor of its full-year capital expenditures.
Free cash flow came in at a negative $2.12 billion during the quarter.
Meta said it expects its full-year capex to range from $135 billion to $145 billion, raising the bottom of the range from a previous $130 billion.

The spread on the social media giant's five-year credit default swaps reached all-time highs on Thursday, a signal of growing credit concerns from investors as the company leans deeper into its artificial intelligence spending plans.
